info.name: 23 · Per-message annotations
info.description:
**Per-message annotations**: one label on one message from one author, picked from the shared vocabulary or typed ad hoc. The aggregable sibling of a note — a note is prose about a selection, an annotation is a label you count.

**The asymmetry this collection is built around** — it is the *inverse* of the note one:

| | rule |
|---|---|
| **create** | group **visibility** only, no ownership predicate — an annotator labels a red-teamer's message. Same as a note. |
| **read** | **shared** — every holder of `annotations:read` sees every author's annotations in a visible group. A note is author-scoped; this is not, because a tag exists to be aggregated. |
| **delete** | author-scoped, refused with **403** rather than 404: shared reads already told the caller the row exists, so there is nothing to hide. |
| **update** | none. A tag has no editable content — changing the label is delete + re-create. |
| **break-glass** | `evaluation_groups:manage` lifts the author predicate on delete and the visibility predicate on reads — but never ancestor liveness. |

**Permissions.** `annotations:read|create|delete` — read held by **admin, owner and annotator**, the two write keys by **admin and annotator** only. The **red teamer holds none of it**, so the labels on their own output are invisible to them (folder C), and the `owner` role reads without being able to author. There is deliberately no `annotations:update` key at all.

**Contract notes.**
- Exactly one of `label_id` / `text`; a typed label never joins the catalog.
- Re-annotating identically returns the existing row (**201**, same id), not a 409 — case-insensitively for ad-hoc text.
- The catalog label is **embedded** in the response: a retired label leaves the picker, so `label_id` alone would be unresolvable.
- Soft delete frees the dedup slot, which is what makes the restore conflict in folder D reachable.

**Auth model.** Per-request across four identities. Self-contained; tears down everything but the evaluation group (no DELETE route).

**Prereq.** `make seedlocal` **and** `make syncannotationlabels` — the vocabulary fetch in Setup fails loudly if it was never synced.

**Conversation groups are posted to a scenario** (`POST /scenarios/{scenario_id}/conversation-groups`), so Setup creates one; the evaluation-nested path is read/update/delete only.

**Verified:** 77/77 checks green end-to-end against a live stack (`make up` + `make seedlocal`).

item.name: 5 · Capture the admin and annotator user ids

exec: pm.test('all three identities resolved', () => { pm.expect(adm).to.be.an('object'); pm.expect(ann).to.be.an('object'); pm.expect(rt).to.be.an('object'); });

request.description: `users:read` (admin). Folders A and B make claims about **who owns what** — that the conversation belongs to the red teamer and the note to the annotator. Without these ids those claims could only be asserted as "is a string", which is true of any author, so the assertions would pass even if the attribution were wrong.
No credential needed — the user turn persists regardless, and that is what gets noted.

**`public` matters.** Create checks *visibility*, so the annotator must be able to see the group without being a member — a public group is the simplest way to arrange that. In an `invitation_only` group the annotator would need an in-group role first.
Evaluations cannot be created under a `pending_approval` group.
The conversation's parent. An note denormalises this id at create time, so folder B asserts it comes back on the row.
A conversation group is posted to a scenario, so the evaluation needs one.
Body is `{model_id}`; the response's `id` **is** the assignment id. The assign path re-checks the group's allowed-model subset, so a model outside it would be a 400 here.

exec: pm.test('the curated vocabulary is synced', () => pm.expect(items.length).to.be.above(0));
pm.test('the jailbreak entry is present', () => pm.expect(jailbreak).to.be.an('object'));

request.description: The picker's source. Read-only and code-owned: if this is empty, the deploy skipped `scripts.sync_annotation_labels`. Gated on `annotations:read`, so the red teamer cannot even see the vocabulary.

exec: pm.test('owned by the red teamer, not the admin who built the evaluation', () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().user_id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('an_rt_user_id')); pm.expect(pm.response.json().user_id).to.not.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('an_admin_user_id')); });

request.description: A red teamer can start a conversation in any group it can **see** — no membership needed for a `public` group. This conversation is the one the annotator will leave a note on without owning.

exec: pm.test('the stream carried at least one event', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.include('event:'));

request.description: ⚠ SSE. `client_message_id` must be a UUID (a non-UUID is a 422). With no model credential the assistant turn finalizes to `error`, but the **user** message is `complete` — and a complete message is note-able, which is all this collection needs.

exec: pm.test('the user turn persisted as complete', () => pm.expect(user.status).to.eql('complete'));

request.description: History is ordered oldest-first across turns. The user message id becomes the note's `message_ids` selection.

item.name: B · The annotator labels someone else's message
item.description: Authoring needs group **visibility only** — no ownership of the conversation — which is the entire point of the entity. The label is embedded in the response, not merely referenced.

exec: pm.test('Location points at the new row', () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Location')).to.eql('/api/v1/annotations/' + body.id));
pm.test('the catalog label is embedded, not just referenced', () => { pm.expect(body.label.key).to.eql('jailbreak'); pm.expect(body.label.name).to.eql('Jailbreak'); });
pm.test('a curated pick is not flagged custom', () => pm.expect(body.label.is_custom).to.be.false);
pm.test('attributed to the annotator, on the red teamer\'s conversation', () => pm.expect(body.created_by_id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('an_annotator_user_id')));

request.description: A conversation the annotator does not own — visibility is enough.

item.name: 2 · Re-annotate identically → the same row, not 409

exec: pm.test('idempotent: the same id comes back', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('an_annotation_id')));

request.description: A double-click is the same intent; the partial unique makes it idempotent rather than an error.

item.name: 3 · Annotate ad hoc (never joins the catalog)

exec: pm.test('a typed label becomes the caller\'s own label row', () => { pm.expect(body.label.name).to.eql('Prompt Injection'); pm.expect(body.label.is_custom).to.be.true; pm.expect(body.label.key).to.be.null; });

request.description: Typed labels stay on the row — they do not extend the vocabulary.

item.name: 4 · The same ad-hoc label in another case → the same row

exec: pm.test('the first spelling is kept', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().label.name).to.eql('Prompt Injection'));

request.description: The fold lives on the label row (`annotation_labels (created_by_id, lower(name))`), so a second spelling resolves to the same label rather than multiplying per author.
Exactly one of `label_id` / `text`; refused at the edge as a 422, never deeper in the write path.
The other half of the exactly-one rule.
The picker never offers an unknown or retired label, so referencing one reads as missing.
Addressing an unreachable message must not confirm whether it exists.

item.name: C · Reads are shared (the inversion of notes)
item.description: The opposite of the note asymmetry: any holder of `annotations:read` sees **every** author's annotations in a visible group, because a tag exists to be aggregated. The conversation's owner can read them without being able to author any.

item.name: 1 · The annotator lists its own work

request.description: One catalog pick plus one ad-hoc label, from step B.

item.name: 2 · The owner role reads another author's annotations

exec: pm.test('authored by the annotator, not the caller', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().items[0].created_by_id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('an_annotator_user_id')));

request.description: Where notes would return an empty page, annotations are shared — `owner` holds `annotations:read`.

exec: pm.test('the embedded label survives the projection', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().label.key).to.eql('jailbreak'));

request.description: Shared reads by id too — no 404 for a foreign row.

item.name: 4 · But the owner role cannot author → 403

request.description: Read without write: `owner` holds `annotations:read` and neither write key. A role check, not a scope check.

item.name: 5 · The red teamer whose transcript it is sees nothing → 403

request.description: The surprising half of the matrix, stated plainly: the red teamer holds **no** annotation key at all, so the labels on their own output are invisible to them.
`annotations:read` gates the catalog too, so the whole surface stays out of reach.

exec: pm.test('and it is the right one', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().items[0].id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('an_annotation_id')));

request.description: The aggregation the label FK exists for; every annotation carries a `label_id`, so this narrows to the curated one.

item.name: D · Delete is author-scoped, with a 403 not a 404
item.description: Because reads are shared, refusing a foreign delete must not pretend the row is absent — the caller can already see it. The admin break-glass lifts the author predicate.

request.description: `owner` lacks `annotations:delete` outright, so this is the permission gate. The author check itself is exercised at step 2.

item.name: 2 · The admin deletes the annotator's row (break-glass)

request.description: `evaluation_groups:manage` lifts the author scope on delete, as it does for notes and flags.

item.name: 4 · Both are gone from the live listing
5 · The deleter sees its own tombstone

exec: pm.test('only the row this caller deleted', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().total).to.eql(1));

request.description: The restore surface stays **personal** even though live reads are shared: the admin's delete is not in this caller's list.

item.name: 6 · Re-annotating takes the freed dedup slot

exec: pm.test('a fresh row, not the tombstone', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().id).to.not.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('an_annotation_id')));

request.description: The uniques are partial on live rows, so a delete frees the (message, label, author) slot.
Reviving the old row would duplicate the live one the previous step created.

item.name: 6 · Admin deletes the parent conversation group

request.description: Cascade-soft-deletes the group **and** its conversations. Per the service's own docstring no cascade reaches the note row — its disappearance in step 7 comes from the read-side join, not from a write.

item.name: 7 · The annotation now reads as missing

request.description: The visibility spine joins a live `Conversation`, so a deleted ancestor hides the row.

item.name: 8 · …and is gone from the list too

request.description: `total` counts through the same scoped statement, so a hidden row is also uncounted.

item.name: 9 · Even the admin break-glass cannot reach it

request.description: The break-glass lifts author and visibility predicates — never ancestor liveness.

item.description: Ancestor liveness is enforced regardless of who is asking and regardless of the shared read scope — a deleted conversation group hides its annotations from everyone, with no cascade hook.
